draft.title: Where a function is not differentiable
card: A derivative at a point is the gradient of the tangent there. If no single tangent gradient exists, the function is not differentiable at that point.
the left and right sides have different gradients. For f(x) = |x| at x = 0, the gradient is −1 on the left and 1 on the right, so there is no derivative.
the graph breaks, so it is not continuous there. A function that is not continuous at a point cannot be differentiable there.

the tangent is a vertical line, which has no gradient. For f(x) = ∛x at x = 0, the curve is continuous but the gradient grows without limit. So a function can be continuous at a point and still not differentiable there.
draft.remember: No derivative where the graph has a corner, a jump or a vertical tangent.

a.q: Which function is continuous at x = 0 but has no derivative there?
a.why: The graph of |x| has no break at x = 0, but the gradient changes from −1 to 1 at the corner, so there is no derivative. The graph of x² is smooth at x = 0, with gradient 0, so it is differentiable.
a.clue: Look for the function whose graph has a sharp point at the origin.

b.q: A function has gradient 2 for x < 3 and gradient 2 for x > 3, but its graph jumps up by 4 units at x = 3. What is true at x = 3?
opts: It is not differentiable, because it is not continuous
It is differentiable, because both gradients equal 2
It is not differentiable, because of a sharp corner
It is not differentiable, because the tangent is vertical
b.why: A jump means the function is not continuous at x = 3, so it cannot be differentiable there. Equal gradients on each side are tempting, but the two pieces do not meet, so there is no single tangent at that point.
b.clue: Check whether the graph is joined at x = 3 before comparing gradients.

b.best: It is not differentiable, because it is not continuous
